classification.difficultyReason: Order each list, apply the taught odd- or even-sized median-of-halves rule, average central pairs where needed, and subtract to obtain range and IQR. The choice of positions is routine and explicitly taught.

content.prompt: Find the range and interquartile range of each data set.

answer.worked:
Ordered data: $3,5,7,7,10,13,15,15,20$.

The median is $10$. Omit it to form the lower half $3,5,7,7$ and upper half $13,15,15,20$.

$$\begin{align*}Q_1&=\frac{5+7}{2}=6\\Q_3&=\frac{15+15}{2}=15\\\text{Range}&=20-3=17\\\text{IQR}&=15-6=9\end{align*}$$

Ordered data: $1,5,5,5,7,7,7,8,8,10$.

Divide into two equal halves: $1,5,5,5,7$ and $7,7,8,8,10$. Each half contains five values, so its third value is its median.

$$\begin{align*}Q_1&=5\\Q_3&=8\\\text{Range}&=10-1=9\\\text{IQR}&=8-5=3\end{align*}$$

Ordered data: $0,4,4,4,6,6,7,9$.

Divide into two equal halves: $0,4,4,4$ and $6,6,7,9$. Average the two middle values of each half.

$$\begin{align*}Q_1&=\frac{4+4}{2}=4\\Q_3&=\frac{6+7}{2}=6.5\\\text{Range}&=9-0=9\\\text{IQR}&=6.5-4=2.5\end{align*}$$

Ordered data: $1,3,5,8,11,13,13,18$.

Divide into two equal halves: $1,3,5,8$ and $11,13,13,18$. Average the two middle values of each half.

$$\begin{align*}Q_1&=\frac{3+5}{2}=4\\Q_3&=\frac{13+13}{2}=13\\\text{Range}&=18-1=17\\\text{IQR}&=13-4=9\end{align*}$$
